DIRECTION C

Technical Blueprint · Signal Layer

A cool blueprint canvas printed with a faint cyan grid. The chrome is white — not dark — separated from the canvas by a single 1 px cyan baseline. Domain accents become first-class orientation strips on every region edge. The result reads like a drafting board: precise, scaled, instrument-grade.

What stays grey · what becomes chrome · ink · colour

Chrome. White chrome (#FAFCFD), separated from the cool blueprint canvas (#E6EDF1) by a single 1 px cyan rule. Chrome is light here, not dark. Every chrome region exposes the colour identity of the active mode group via a 4 px vertical domain strip.

Ink. Ink #0E1E2C — deeper than ordinary black, faintly cyan-shifted to sit cleanly against the cool canvas. Mono is used aggressively for any structured data — hostnames, IPs, IDs, deltas, timestamps. Micro labels uppercase 9.5 px with strong tracking.

Colour. Drafting cyan #0E72A0 is the instrument signal. It is the colour of focus rings, primary actions, active sub-nav underlines, the highlight on matched search substrings, panel header rules, and the divider between chrome and canvas. It is never used for status or domain — those are different colour systems.

Implementation risks

Grid noise. The blueprint grid is 0.045 alpha on a cool background — at 100% scale it is invisible, at scaled-down screenshots it can disappear entirely. Keep the grid; document that it is a 96 dpi affordance, not a print artefact.
Cyan = Foundation collision. Foundation domain colour is identical to the signal cyan by design. Verify the rail looks right when a Foundation mode is active: the active glow (cyan) and the group strip (also cyan) must read as a coherent assembly, not as colour stacking. May need a 1-stop hue shift on Foundation if it fails the eye test.
White-on-white density. White chrome on white panels needs every divider to do work. The 1 px lines must be #C8D5DE or stronger — anything lighter and the regions melt together. We are spending contrast budget on lines, not surfaces.
Print parity. Blueprint canvas screenshots well and prints well — the design language already maps onto Assess report PDFs. Slight positive: this direction is the cheapest to extend into print artefacts.

Surface treatments

  • TitleBar. White chrome with a single 1 px cyan rule at the bottom — the only place the cyan signal touches the titlebar. Brand mark on the left; domain pill uses the soft cyan tint for Foundation, full domain colour for others. No machined-edge effect — type drives the identity here, not material.
  • ModeRail. Cool light grey (#ECF1F4) — slightly cooler than the canvas. Group headers carry a 4 px domain orientation strip on the left, full-bleed top-to-bottom of the group. Active row gets a cyan left border and a selected-blue background — minimal, scope-changing.
  • Context Sidebar. White panel. Header carries a 4 px cyan leading strip. Active row gets an inset 3 px cyan border instead of a fill — so the sidebar can stay quiet while the active row stays unambiguous. Kind sections use uppercase micro labels with cyan colour.
  • Cortex overlay. White card with a 3 px cyan top border — the launcher reads like an inserted drafting layer over the blueprint. Matched substrings get a cyan tint background instead of bold weight. The scrim is shallow because the canvas underneath is already cool and quiet.
  • Dashboard cards. White panel + 5 px domain strip on the left. Panel header gets an uppercase tracked title, separated from the body by a cyan 1 px rule. KPI values in mono. Domain dot + small label leads every metric. Charts use cyan strokes with very light fills; everything else stays ink.

State semantics

Capability states are signal-grade and reserved. Critical is the only saturated red and only appears on actively failing items. Blocked rows render with the label inked red; deferred rows render italic + muted; partial cards get an amber leading bar.

Domain accents

Domain accents are elevated to first-class navigational marks — wider strips (4–5 px), full-height, on the rail group and the left of every dashboard card. Foundation deliberately shares its hue with the drafting-cyan signal: foundation is the system layer; cyan is the instrument layer; they cousin-rhyme on purpose.
